stories.title: DRAM prices double in 2026 as AI focus squeezes PC makers
stories.summary: Contract prices for DRAM have doubled throughout 2026 as AI server demand consumes disproportionate manufacturing capacity, particularly for high-bandwidth memory variants that command premium pricing. PC and smartphone manufacturers face acute component shortages and cost pressures, with some vendors reducing DRAM content in consumer devices to preserve margins.
stories.why_it_matters: The DRAM supply squeeze is transferring profitability from consumer electronics to AI infrastructure supply chains, forcing PC and smartphone makers to either absorb margin compression or pass costs to price-sensitive consumers. This dynamic risks slowing consumer device refresh cycles and innovation, while memory manufacturers' allocation decisions toward AI-grade products may permanently restructure the semiconductor industry's revenue balance between computing and memory segments.
stories.title_zh: DRAM prices double in 2026 as AI focus squeezes PC makers
stories.summary_zh: 2026年全年DRAM合同价格翻了一番，因为AI服务器需求消耗了不成比例的制造产能，特别是定价溢价的高带宽内存变体。PC和智能手机制造商面临严重的组件短缺和成本压力，一些供应商减少消费设备中的DRAM内容以保持利润率。
stories.why_zh: DRAM供应挤压正在将盈利能力从消费电子转移到AI基础设施供应链，迫使PC和智能手机制造商要么吸收利润压缩，要么将成本转嫁给价格敏感的消费者。这种动态可能会减缓消费设备更新周期和创新，而内存制造商向AI级产品的分配决策可能会永久性地重构半导体行业在计算和内存领域之间的收入平衡。
stories.content:

# DRAM prices double in 2026 as AI focus squeezes PC makers

stories.title: Vertiv opens Singapore centre for AI infrastructure
stories.summary: The new facility provides a testing environment where operators can validate integrated liquid cooling, power distribution, and thermal management systems under simulated AI workload conditions up to 100 kW per rack. Vertiv's investment responds to urgent customer demand for pre-deployment verification as failures in live AI environments carry catastrophic financial and reputational costs.
stories.why_it_matters: Singapore's emergence as an AI infrastructure testing hub concentrates vendor and operator expertise in a location with strict regulatory standards, creating knowledge spillovers that elevate regional technical capabilities. Competitors like Schneider Electric and Huawei must now match this local presence or risk exclusion from early-stage design decisions as Asian operators increasingly demand hands-on validation before committing to multi-million dollar infrastructure deployments.
stories.title_zh: Vertiv在新加坡开设AI基础设施中心
stories.summary_zh: 新设施提供了一个测试环境，运营商可以在模拟AI工作负载条件下验证集成的液冷、电力分配和热管理系统，每机架高达100 kW。Vertiv的投资回应了客户对部署前验证的迫切需求，因为在实时AI环境中失败会带来灾难性的财务和声誉成本。
stories.why_zh: 新加坡作为AI基础设施测试中心的崛起将供应商和运营商的专业知识集中在具有严格监管标准的地点，创造知识溢出效应，提升区域技术能力。Schneider Electric和Huawei等竞争对手现在必须匹配这一本地存在，否则随着亚洲运营商越来越要求在承诺数百万美元基础设施部署之前进行实际操作验证，他们可能会被排除在早期设计决策之外。
stories.content:
Tue, 3rd Nov 2026 (Today)
Vertiv has opened the Vertiv Experience Centre Singapore, a facility for customers and partners working on AI and high-density computing infrastructure.

The new centre gives visitors hands-on access to the company's integrated power, liquid cooling and infrastructure systems. It is designed for customers, channel partners, consultants and other industry stakeholders.

The facility features live demonstrations of intelligent modular data centre infrastructure, thermal management equipment, power management systems and monitoring tools. It shows how those technologies work together in environments built for AI and dense computing workloads.

Featured systems include Vertiv SmartRun, a prefabricated overhead infrastructure product that combines power distribution, liquid cooling piping, networking and busway in a single platform. The site also includes Vertiv SmartAisle 3, described by the company as its latest generation of modular data centre infrastructure.

Other technologies on show include liquid cooling systems for direct-to-chip and other high-density cooling applications, as well as critical power systems, switchgear and power distribution equipment. Visitors can also see infrastructure management and monitoring systems designed to give operators greater visibility over site conditions and operations.

Singapore is one of Asia's main digital infrastructure hubs, and the opening comes as AI workloads increase pressure on data centre operators to manage rising power density and cooling demand. Across the sector, suppliers have been expanding their offerings in liquid cooling, power management and integrated infrastructure as operators adapt facilities for more intensive computing loads.

Antony Szafranek, Senior Director for Strategic Accounts, Vertiv Asia, said the new centre reflects changing customer requirements across the region. "Organisations across Asia are scaling their digital infrastructure to support AI innovation, creating new demands for reliability, efficiency and speed of deployment," Szafranek said.

He added: "The Experience Centre gives customers and partners a hands-on environment to explore how integrated power and cooling technologies can support higher-density computing while maintaining operational resilience."

### AI infrastructure

The centre is intended to illustrate an end-to-end approach to AI infrastructure spanning power, cooling and IT systems. That focus mirrors a broader industry push to link electrical, thermal and computing design more closely as AI servers consume more energy and generate more heat than conventional enterprise systems.

Daniel Sim, Senior Director for AI Ecosystem Alliances and Channel Partners, Vertiv Asia, said customers need to assess how those elements work together rather than in isolation. "The pace of AI-driven transformation requires greater integration of power, cooling and IT infrastructure," Sim said.

He added: "At the Experience Centre, customers can see how these technologies work together to address the infrastructure requirements of AI and high-density computing."

Vertiv, which is listed in New York, sells power, cooling and IT infrastructure products for data centres, communications networks and industrial facilities. It says it operates in more than 130 countries.

stories.title_zh: 铜、锡随基本金属下跌，因AI股票新一轮抛售削弱需求前景
stories.content:
(Nov 3): Copper and tin fell with other industrial metals, as a renewed sell-off in technology stocks in Asia weakened the demand outlook for materials used in data centres and to solder circuit boards.

Both contracts dropped more than 1% on the London Metal Exchange as concerns persisted over spending and stretched valuations at artificial intelligence companies. Tin has plunged 10% this quarter, the worst performer among the LME’s six major metals.

Copper had risen on Monday, helped in part by a pullback in oil prices that could mitigate inflation pressures. The US and Iran have signalled a willingness to pursue peace talks, easing anxiety over the war’s impact on interest rates and global growth.

Still, macro conditions are putting a lot of pressure on metals, particularly given the possibility that the conflict could resume after the US midterm elections, said Xu Wanqiu, an analyst with Cofco Futures Co.

Copper fell 1.2% to US$14,180 a tonne as of 10.50am in Shanghai (same time as Malaysia) while tin declined 2.2% to US$48,550 a tonne. Aluminium dropped 1.1% to US$3,060.50 a tonne.

stories.title: Supporting Efficient and Resilient Data Centre Growth Across Asia Pacific
stories.summary: Regional operators are confronting simultaneous pressures to expand capacity rapidly for AI workloads while maintaining 99.999% uptime commitments and accelerating net-zero carbon timelines. The convergence of these demands is forcing fundamental architectural decisions about power sourcing, cooling technology, and facility design that will determine competitive positioning for the next decade.
stories.why_it_matters: The triple constraint of speed, reliability, and sustainability is creating a bifurcation between operators with capital and technical depth to optimize across all three dimensions versus those forced to sacrifice one priority for another. This dynamic favors integrated players with in-house engineering and long-term power contracting capabilities, while squeezing mid-tier colocation providers who lack scale to negotiate renewable energy deals or invest in advanced cooling research.
stories.title_zh: 支持亚太地区高效且具韧性的数据中心增长
stories.summary_zh: 区域运营商面临着同时为AI工作负载快速扩展容量、保持99.999%正常运行时间承诺和加速净零碳时间表的压力。这些需求的融合正在迫使关于电力采购、冷却技术和设施设计的基本架构决策，这些决策将决定未来十年的竞争定位。
stories.why_zh: 速度、可靠性和可持续性的三重约束正在造成分化：一方是拥有资本和技术深度以在所有三个维度上进行优化的运营商，另一方是被迫为一个优先事项牺牲另一个的运营商。这种动态有利于拥有内部工程能力和长期电力合同能力的整合型玩家，同时挤压缺乏规模来谈判可再生能源交易或投资先进冷却研究的中端colocation提供商。
stories.content:
Artificial intelligence may be digital, but the infrastructure behind it is highly physical, and increasingly energy intensive. Across the Asia Pacific region, continued investment in digital infrastructure is reshaping the data center landscape. Analysts such as Moody's project the region's data center market could reach $800 billion by 2030 as operators expand capacity to support more compute-intensive workloads.

As demands grow, data center operators are balancing multiple priorities at once: scaling capacity, maintaining uptime, improving energy efficiency and supporting broader sustainability goals. Cooling plays a central role in that equation, particularly as operators work to manage increasingly dense computing environments and more complex thermal loads.

"The industry is facing dual pressure: meeting the massive compute demands of the AI era while advancing ambitious decarbonization goals," said Sharad Yadav, president, North and Southeast Asia, Trane Technologies. "As data center requirements continue to evolve, customers are looking for cooling strategies that can support performance, efficiency and reliability over the long term."

### Expanding Cooling Capabilities

To help meet these evolving needs, global climate innovator Trane Technologies has continued to expand its data center thermal management capabilities in recent years. With cooling representing a significant share of a facility's total energy use, the company's high-efficiency and reliable solutions can help support uninterrupted 24/7 operations while advancing customers' stringent Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) goals.

Yadav noted that customers increasingly need more than durable equipment alone. They are also looking for innovation that can keep pace with rapid changes in compute density, facility design and operational requirements.

To strengthen these capabilities, Trane Technologies has expanded its portfolio through recent acquisitions of specialized companies, including LiquidStack, an innovator in advanced liquid cooling for AI workloads, and Stellar Energy, known for its modular turnkey solutions. In parallel, Trane is collaborating with chip manufacturers to optimize cooling designs and improve thermal management performance for large-scale AI factories.

### Addressing Regional Heat and Space Constraints

Data center operators across Asia Pacific face a wide range of infrastructure challenges. In high-growth markets such as India and Indonesia, rapid capacity expansion is often taking place in climates that place significant demands on equipment performance. In land-constrained markets such as Japan and Singapore, operators may need to maximize computing capacity within smaller footprints, making retrofit strategies and space-efficient system design increasingly important.

To help customers navigate these market-specific conditions, Trane Technologies, through its strategic brand Trane, draws on a broad portfolio rather than applying a one-size-fits-all approach. In hotter environments, its advanced air-cooled chillers are engineered to support stable performance even in demanding ambient temperatures. In space-constrained settings, compact solutions such as fan wall units help maximize cooling performance within a smaller footprint, enabling customers to use white space more efficiently.

At the same time, as generative AI drives higher rack densities, Trane is helping customers evaluate and transition to next-generation cooling solutions. These include technologies such as magnetic bearing centrifugal chillers which enhance energy efficiency through frictionless, oil-free operation, and Trane's first locally-developed coolant distribution unit (CDU) for Asia Pacific, designed to deliver precise liquid cooling to high-density compute environments.

### A System-Level Approach for a Changing Market

As data center requirements become more complex, customers are looking for integrated approaches that balance efficiency, reliability and sustainability. That includes not only the cooling equipment, but also how systems are designed, deployed and optimized for different operating environments.

"Customers across the region are no longer looking for standalone equipment; they need a comprehensive system that balances high efficiency, low carbon emissions, and reliability," Yadav said.

Across Asia Pacific, operators are under pressure to add capacity without compromising performance, efficiency or long-term resilience. In that environment, cooling strategy is becoming a critical part of data center design and operation, and Trane Technologies is helping customers navigate that shift with solutions tailored to regional and operational needs.

stories.title: Vietnam's province considers US$700 million AI data center project
stories.summary: The proposed facility at Nam Tan Uyen Industrial Park would represent one of Vietnam's largest foreign-invested data center projects, with the consortium targeting AI training and inference workloads. Tay Ninh Province's proximity to Ho Chi Minh City offers strategic positioning for serving southern Vietnam's growing digital economy while potentially accessing submarine cable landing stations.
stories.why_it_matters: Vietnam's emergence as a credible alternative to Singapore and Malaysia for large-scale AI infrastructure depends on provincial governments delivering reliable power and streamlined approvals. Tay Ninh's consideration of this project tests whether Vietnamese industrial zones can match the execution certainty that hyperscalers require, with success likely triggering competing proposals from Da Nang and Hanoi regions seeking similar investment inflows.
stories.title_zh: 越南某省考虑7亿美元AI数据中心项目
stories.summary_zh: 拟议的位于Nam Tan Uyen Industrial Park的设施将成为越南最大的外国投资data centre项目之一，该财团瞄准AI训练和推理工作负载。Tay Ninh省靠近Ho Chi Minh City，为服务越南南部不断增长的数字经济提供了战略位置，同时可能接入海底电缆登陆站。
stories.why_zh: 越南作为新加坡和马来西亚大规模AI基础设施的可信替代品的出现，取决于省级政府能否提供可靠的电力和简化的审批。Tay Ninh对该项目的考虑正在测试越南工业园区是否能匹配hyperscalers所需的执行确定性，成功可能会触发Da Nang和Hanoi地区寻求类似投资流入的竞争性提案。
stories.content:
Tay Ninh Province in Vietnam is considering a proposed US$ 700 million artificial intelligence data center project following discussions with Taiwan’s World Vision United Group and its international partners.

The proposal, involving an investment consortium led by SAIGONTEL, would cover 20 hectares at Nam Tan Uyen Industrial Park. The planned facility would have a capacity of 200 MW, with the first phase accounting for 100 MW as reported by Saigon Giai Phone.

A delegation from Vietnam’s Tay Ninh Province recently visited Taipei, Taiwan, to survey the YiDi project in Datong District and hold discussions with World Vision United Group and its international partners. During a working session, the investors presented the project proposal to provincial officials, outlining its proposed scale and investment.

According to Tay Ninh authorities the project could support the development of the local digital economy and attract high-tech investment. However, the province will hold further discussions with the investors to assess the project’s feasibility.

The next stage will focus on clarifying requirements for infrastructure, power supply and technology, as well as the proposed investment scale and implementation schedule.

stories.title: Perak and Global Vision Lab look into opening new AI data centre in the state
stories.summary: Perak State Development Corporation is evaluating a proposal from Global Vision Lab for an AI-focused data center development, potentially leveraging the state's relatively lower land and power costs compared to the saturated Klang Valley market. The discussions represent Perak's strategic effort to attract technology investment and diversify from traditional manufacturing and agriculture dependence.
stories.why_it_matters: Malaysia's data center geography is fragmenting beyond the established Cyberjaya and Iskandar corridors as states compete for AI investment with differentiated incentive packages. Perak's entry disrupts the pricing power of incumbent developers in saturated markets while testing whether secondary Malaysian locations can deliver the fiber connectivity and grid reliability that hyperscale customers require without excessive infrastructure buildout delays.

stories.title_zh: Perak与Global Vision Lab探讨在该州新建AI数据中心
stories.summary_zh: Perak State Development Corporation正在评估Global Vision Lab的AI-focused data centre开发提案，可能利用该州相对于饱和的Klang Valley市场较低的土地和电力成本。这些讨论代表了Perak吸引技术投资并从传统制造业和农业依赖中多元化的战略努力。
stories.why_zh: 随着各州以差异化激励方案竞争AI投资，马来西亚的data centre地理正在超越成熟的Cyberjaya和Iskandar走廊而碎片化。Perak的进入扰乱了饱和市场中现有开发商的定价权，同时测试二级马来西亚地点能否在不产生过度基础设施建设延迟的情况下提供hyperscale客户所需的光纤连接和电网可靠性。
stories.content:
KUALA LUMPUR (Nov 3): The Perak State Development Corporation (PKNPk) and Global Vision Lab Sdn Bhd (GVL) are exploring a proposal for an artificial intelligence (AI) data centre development in Perak.

So far, only a non-disclosure agreement and a letter of consent have been signed so both parties can exchange information and hold preliminary assessments for the project.

This data centre would be used to meet the growing demand for AI computing, high–performance computing and graphics processing unit-based applications across Malaysia and the region, with a planned power capacity exceeding 100MW.

As the initiative is still in the preliminary assessment phase, the full scope and power capacity is still to be determined.

Under the agreement, PKNPk will be in charge of coordinating state-level stakeholders while GVL leads the development planning and assessments.

Itman Service Center (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd and Future Quantum Co Ltd have also been mentioned as project partners, though their roles are yet to be finalised.

This proposal is part of an effort to strengthen Perak’s role in Malaysia’s digital ecosystem. The preliminary assessment is to focus on site suitability, power supply availability, cooling system, network connectivity and related infrastructure requirements.

“The initiative supports the aspirations of Perak Sejahtera 2030 and creates opportunities for Perak to emerge as a destination for the development of high-technology digital infrastructure,” said PKNPk chief executive Datuk Redza Rafiq in a release.

Additionally, the data centre could also bring high-skilled job opportunities, strengthen local supply chains and increase AI adoption across sectors.

stories.title: Power regulators now decide AI data centre locations
stories.summary: The decisive say over AI data centre siting is shifting from local planners to energy regulators and central governments, impacting project timelines. This trend is evident in Australia, Canada, and the UK, where large AI campuses face new hurdles for approvals and grid access.
stories.title_zh: 电力监管机构现在决定AI数据中心选址
stories.content:
The approval process for AI data centres is increasingly being controlled by energy regulators and central governments, a shift that is setting the pace for new infrastructure builds.Project Ares, a planned 1GW AI data centre in Australia's Northern Territory, has lost its June 2028 first-power date, Reuters reported. Energy North, the developer, called the date "indicative" and awaits terms for an environmental impact statement from the Northern Territory Environment Protection Authority (NT EPA). The NT EPA suspended its seven-week deadline to seek advice from the federal government, which is still developing data centre policy.The regulator identified 10 potential impacts from the roughly 190 sq km campus, ranging from water strain to disruption of Aboriginal sacred sites. It expressed low confidence that proposed measures would manage significant impacts.
### North American and UK Shifts

In Alberta, Canada, the Alberta Utilities Commission (AUC) approved a 920MW gas plant to supply Beacon Data Centers' Heartland hub in Sturgeon County. However, the decision on the associated 800MW data centre itself is pending, The Globe and Mail reported.Opposition is growing in Alberta, with landowners contesting Beacon's gas plant plans near Indus and Samson Cree Nation considering its next steps. Ontario's Oakville has also imposed the province's first data centre moratorium.The UK has implemented a Data Centre Covenant, published with Chancellor John Healey’s 28 October Budget, setting five tests for strategic data centres. These tests cover energy costs, community investment, environmental standards, jobs, and security.Strategic data centres that pass these tests may receive reserved or reallocated grid capacity, with exceptional sites potentially getting temporary on-site generation. A Ministerial Control Centre, chaired by the minister for AI, will determine qualifying sites, but the government has not yet defined a "strategic data centre". Microsoft previously withdrew from Nscale's planned Loughton site after being informed grid power might not arrive until the early-to-mid 2030s.
### Financial Sector Adapts

The financial sector is adapting to these extended timelines, with insurers, brokers, and industry bodies in Singapore developing a regional data centre insurance facility. This facility will have US$200 million of initial capacity and cover construction, operations, supply chain, design, and cyber risks, national development minister Chee Hong Tat said on 2 November. Asia-Pacific data centre capacity is about 32GW, projected to reach 57GW by 2030.

- Policy, Land & Power
- 2 min Read

# Power regulators now decide AI data centre locations

The decisive say over AI data centre siting is shifting from local planners to energy regulators and central governments, impacting project timelines. This trend is evident in Australia, Canada, and the UK, where large AI campuses face new hurdles for approvals and grid access.

- Published On Nov 03, 2026 at 07:50 AM IST

## Highlights

- Australia's Project Ares, a 1GW AI data centre, lost its 2028 start date due to regulatory delays.
- Canada's Alberta Utilities Commission approved a gas plant for Beacon Data Centers, but not the data centre.
- The UK's Data Centre Covenant offers grid priority to strategic sites, yet definitions remain unclear.
- Singapore is developing a US$200 million insurance facility for data centre risks amid project delays.

stories.title: Oracle taps investors for US$20 billion to finance AI expansion
stories.summary: Oracle seeks to more than triple its revenue by fiscal 2030
stories.title_zh: Oracle向投资者融资200亿美元以资助AI扩张
stories.content:
Oracle seeks to more than triple its revenue by fiscal 2030

ORACLE plans to raise US$20 billion through bond and share sales, regulatory filings showed on Monday (Nov 2), as the software giant taps investors to fund its costly AI and cloud infrastructure build-out.

Shares of the company fell 8.8 per cent to US$119.22, bringing their losses this year to about 39 per cent.

Oracle said it would use the proceeds for general corporate purposes, including capital spending, debt repayment, acquisitions, dividends and share buybacks.

The share sale is expected to be priced at US$116 per share, an 11 per cent discount to Friday’s close, Bloomberg News reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

Oracle did not immediately respond to Reuters request for comment.

The fundraising underscores the scale of Oracle’s AI investment as it seeks to more than triple revenue by fiscal 2030.

The company said last week that capital spending would peak this fiscal year and the next, while pledging to raise no more than US$20 billion in additional financing for AI through fiscal 2030.

Shares rallied about 11 per cent on Wednesday after CFO Hilary Maxson said Oracle also expects free cash flow to turn positive in the second half of fiscal 2028.

Oracle had US$125.34 billion in notes payable and other borrowings, as of Aug 31, compared with fiscal 2026 revenue of US$67.36 billion. It expects revenue to exceed US$225 billion and adjusted earnings to top US$21 per share in fiscal 2030.

Wall Street expects the company’s adjusted profit per share for fiscal 2027 to be US$8.14, according to data compiled by LSEG.

The bond offering comprises six tranches maturing between 2029 and 2046, including one floating-rate tranche and five fixed-rate tranches. Interest rates, prices and the number of shares have not been set.

Oracle’s existing 6.85 per cent bonds due in 2066 fell more than 1.2 cents on the dollar, according to Tradeweb data.

Investors have focused on Oracle’s AI spending because it lacks the revenue scale of cloud rivals Microsoft and Amazon and has significant exposure to OpenAI, the loss-making developer of ChatGPT. REUTERS

stories.title: AI is collapsing the boundaries inside modern data centres
stories.summary: The rapid rise of AI is not only driving unprecedented demand for data centres. It is fundamentally changing how those facilities are designed. Legrand’s Head of Data Centre Solutions Brendan Dessent told W.Media that one of the biggest shifts underway is the gradual disappearance of the traditional divide between “grey space” and “white space” inside […]
stories.title_zh: AI正在打破现代数据中心内部的边界
stories.content:
The rapid rise of AI is not only driving unprecedented demand for data centres. It is fundamentally changing how those facilities are designed. Legrand’s Head of Data Centre Solutions Brendan Dessent **told W.Media** that one of the biggest shifts underway is the gradual disappearance of the traditional divide between “grey space” and “white space” inside data centres.

What was once a clear separation between supporting infrastructure and IT equipment is becoming increasingly blurred as AI workloads push compute density to new levels. Historically, white space housed servers and racks, while grey space accommodated the electrical and mechanical infrastructure needed to support them. However, AI-driven deployments are bringing critical infrastructure closer to the rack itself.

Dessent explained that technologies such as rack-level UPS systems, rear-door cooling and closed-loop cooling solutions are moving equipment traditionally located outside the data hall directly into the white space. “The grey space is now not going to be a separate part of the data centre,” he said, describing a future where infrastructure becomes increasingly localised around high-density compute environments.

### AI driving density

The trend is being accelerated by the extraordinary power demands of AI. While data centres have traditionally been designed around relatively modest rack densities, today’s AI environments are pushing rapidly toward 150kW racks, with designs for megawatt-scale racks already being discussed across the industry.

“As rack power climbs, operators can no longer rely on centralised support systems alone,” he said. “Cooling, power protection, and monitoring must become more targeted, more responsive, and physically closer to the equipment being supported.”

“This shift is forcing designers to rethink the data hall itself,” he emphasised.

In one recent example in Australia, electrical infrastructure inside the white space occupied almost the same physical footprint as the rack environment it was supporting, highlighting how support systems are increasingly becoming part of the compute environment rather than separate from it.

### Monitoring becomes mission-critical

With more infrastructure being incorporated into the data hall, operational visibility is becoming increasingly important. As power densities rise and cooling systems become more localised, operators will require far more granular monitoring and management capabilities than in traditional data centre environments.

AI itself is also play a growing role in supporting data centre infrastructure management, as well as generating the reasons for its evolution. Rather than replacing jobs, AI is expected to help project teams handle growing workloads, enabling engineers, estimators, and project managers to manage larger and more complex projects more efficiently.

“There is plenty of work going around,” Dessent said, arguing that AI should be viewed as a capacity multiplier rather than a workforce replacement tool.

### Security challenges emerge

The convergence of infrastructure and computing environments also introduces new security considerations. As mechanical and electrical systems move closer to sensitive computing environments, a larger proportion of maintenance and operations staff may require access to secure areas of facilities. For government and high-security sites, this can involve baseline security clearances and, in some cases, NV1-level security clearances.

The challenge is compounded by Australia’s ongoing shortage of skilled technical workers.

“As we know, we rely in this country a lot on people who aren’t Australian citizens to keep the wheels turning,” Dessent observed.

### The data hall of the future

While debate continues about exactly how far densities can rise, there is broad agreement that AI is driving the industry towards a more integrated model. The future data hall is likely to feature localised power, localised cooling, and highly intelligent monitoring systems, all centred around the rack itself.

In that future, the rack becomes what Dessent described as “the centre of the universe”. Infrastructure will no longer sit around the compute environment. Instead, it will become an inseparable part of it.

If it can, data centres may prove to be more than digital infrastructure. They could become a catalyst for the revitalisation of regional Australia itself.

*This article, **the second of two**, is based on a W.Media interview with Brendan Dessent at the Sydney Cloud & Datacenter Convention 2026 in September. **Listen to the full podcast.***

stories.title: Marvell reaches US$115 billion deal for Lumentum
stories.summary: Marvell's acquisition of Lumentum at a $115 billion enterprise value creates a combined company with end-to-end capabilities in data center optical interconnects, including coherent DSPs, transceivers, and laser components essential for AI cluster scaling. The deal represents one of the largest technology mergers as component suppliers consolidate to capture value from surging AI infrastructure spending.
stories.why_it_matters: The Marvell-Lumentum combination concentrates critical optical component supply under a single vendor, reducing bargaining leverage for cloud providers and systems integrators who must now negotiate with a more powerful supplier. This vertical integration pressure will trigger defensive consolidation among remaining optical players like Coherent and Broadcom, while potentially accelerating Chinese domestic optical component development as geopolitical supply security concerns intensify.

sources.name: The Edge Malaysia — data centre search

stories.title_zh: Marvell 达成以 1150 亿美元收购 Lumentum 的交易
stories.summary_zh: Marvell以1150亿美元企业价值收购Lumentum，创建了一家在data centre光互连领域拥有端到端能力的合并公司，包括AI集群扩展所需的相干DSP、收发器和激光组件。该交易代表了最大的技术合并之一，因为组件供应商整合以从激增的AI基础设施支出中获取价值。
stories.why_zh: Marvell-Lumentum的组合将关键光学组件供应集中在单一供应商之下，减少了云提供商和系统集成商的议价能力，他们现在必须与更强大的供应商谈判。这种垂直整合压力将触发Coherent和Broadcom等剩余光学参与者的防御性整合，同时随着地缘政治供应安全担忧加剧，可能会加速中国国内光学组件开发。
stories.content:
(Nov 2): Marvell Technology Inc has reached a deal to buy data centre optics maker Lumentum Holdings Inc at an enterprise value of US$115 billion (RM466.4 billion), one of the biggest tech tie-ups ever, in a race to capitalise on the artificial intelligence (AI) boom.

The all-stock transaction will give Marvell shareholders 67% of the combined company, according to a statement confirming an earlier *Bloomberg News* report that the two Silicon Valley companies were nearing a pact. The deal is expected to close in the first half of 2028, the companies said.

On an equity basis, it’s the top M&A deal of the year and the largest ever in the global tech sector, excluding the SpaceX-xAI merger, data compiled by *Bloomberg* show. The transaction shows how AI is driving deals across almost all major sectors and regions, from chipmakers and other specialist tech suppliers, to data center operators and power utilities.

Lumentum shares fell as much as 12% in New York to US$740.10. Marvell declined as much as 7.3% to US$182.15. Heading into the announcement, Lumentum was valued at US$76 billion as of Friday. Marvell was valued at US$172.2 billion.

Lumentum makes lasers and other optical technology for moving enormous amounts of data at high speeds. That hardware underpins the AI boom, as it lets data centres and telecommunications firms move information between servers, facilities and other destinations.

Marvell already purchases laser technology from Lumentum, and the larger company has been increasing its bets on optical and photonic technology for connecting data center gear. Earlier this year, Marvell purchased photonics maker Celestial AI.

Nvidia Corp announced an agreement to take a US$2 billion stake in Lumentum in March as part of a deal that included collaboration on photonics, which use light instead of traditional copper wiring to move data faster and more efficiently.

Marvell also works with Amazon.com Inc’s cloud unit and Microsoft Corp to help build custom AI chips. In August, the company struck a chip deal with Alphabet Inc’s Google to support Google’s tensor processing units.

Qatalyst Partners is serving as the lead financial adviser to Marvell, with Goldman Sachs Group Inc and JPMorgan Chase & Co also working with the company. Citigroup Inc and Evercore Inc are advising Lumentum.

stories.title: Northern Solar secures solar-plus-battery projects totalling 189MW for data centres
stories.summary: Northern Solar Holdings Bhd (KL:NORTHERN) has secured two letters of award to supply renewable energy from solar projects with a combined capacity of 189 megawatts (MW), coupled with battery storage systems, to two data centre projects.

sources.name: The Edge Malaysia — data centre search

stories.title_zh: Northern Solar 获得总计 189MW 的数据中心太阳能加储能项目
stories.content:
KUALA LUMPUR (Nov 2): Northern Solar Holdings Bhd (KL:NORTHERN) has secured two letters of award to supply renewable energy from solar projects with a combined capacity of 189 megawatts (MW), coupled with battery storage systems, to two data centre projects.

The awards, received through wholly owned subsidiary Northern Solar Assets Sdn Bhd, fall under the Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme (CRESS), according to the group's filings with Bursa Malaysia on Monday.

The first project involves a 100MW solar facility with a battery energy storage system (BESS) to serve a data centre requiring 262.8 million kilowatt-hours (kWh) of electricity annually.

The second involves an 89MW solar facility, also equipped with BESS, for another data centre with an annual electricity requirement of 233.89 million kWh.

Together, the two data centres have a combined annual electricity requirement of approximately 496.69 million kWh.

Northern Solar did not disclose the value of either project or the identities of the awarding parties, citing confidentiality provisions.

It only said that the first award was issued by a Malaysian company involved in property investment and data centre infrastructure, while the second came from a Malaysian subsidiary of a Singapore-based data centre services operator.

The commencement dates for both projects have yet to be finalised, with further announcements expected upon the signing of definitive agreements.

Northern Solar expects the projects to contribute positively to its earnings and net assets per share during their execution.

The latest awards come as Northern Solar seeks to expand beyond its traditional solar engineering and construction business into owning renewable energy assets.

In September, Apex Securities said the group was finalising details of a potential 170MW solar-plus-storage project under CRESS, which could accelerate its transition towards generating recurring income from long-term electricity supply agreements.

However, it remains unclear whether the two latest awards are related to the project previously highlighted by the research house.

Northern Solar had also secured a RM34 million contract in October to develop a 9.5MW large-scale solar photovoltaic plant, bringing its total contract wins for the year at that point to RM153.4 million.

Its unbilled order book stood at RM189.3 million as at end-June 2026.

Northern Star transferred its listing from Bursa Malaysia's ACE Market to the Main Market on Oct 6.

Its shares closed down four sen or 3.54% at RM1.09 on Monday, valuing the group at RM431.2 million.

stories.title: ISF Group grows order book to RM225.5m with data centre contracts worth RM83.2m
stories.summary: ISF Group Bhd (KL:ISF) has secured four contracts worth a combined RM83.23 million for a hyperscale data centre in Port Dickson, Negeri Sembilan, the largest amount it has announced to date.

sources.name: The Edge Malaysia — data centre search

stories.title_zh: ISF Group 凭借价值 8320 万令吉的数据中心合同将订单增加至 2.255 亿令吉
stories.content:
KUALA LUMPUR (Nov 2): ISF Group Bhd (KL:ISF) has secured four contracts worth a combined RM83.23 million for a hyperscale data centre in Port Dickson, Negeri Sembilan, the largest amount it has announced to date.

The piping solutions provider said its wholly-owned subsidiary Yeo Plumber Sdn Bhd accepted three subcontracts and a letter of award from an unnamed Malaysian construction firm, according to a Bursa filing on Monday.

The three subcontracts are worth RM73.33 million and involve cold water systems, rainwater harvesting, water distribution and sanitary services, while the RM9.9 million letter of award covers external sewerage works.

The projects are scheduled for completion between November 2026 and July 2028.

Following the latest wins, the group's unbilled order book has increased to RM225.5 million, providing earnings visibility through the financial year ending Dec 31, 2029 (FY2029).

ISF managing director Jeff Ai Boon Chen described the contracts as a significant milestone for the group, reflecting its growing ability to undertake larger and more complex projects.

Ai said Malaysia's emergence as a regional data centre hub continues to create opportunities for supporting infrastructure works, with data centre projects accounting for a significant portion of the group's business.

ISF it is also exploring opportunities to expand into larger-scale water infrastructure projects in Malaysia, particularly water treatment plants and initiatives to reduce water losses from supply networks.

The latest contracts follow at least RM47 million in jobs ISF won this year, including a RM14.5 million data centre project in June.

ISF, which made its debut on Bursa Malaysia's ACE Market on Jan 28 at an initial public offering price of 33 sen, is regarded by research house CGS International as an underappreciated stock benefitting from the next wave of data centre construction.

Shares of ISF closed unchanged at 83.5 sen Monday, valuing the group at RM835 million.

stories.title: Envision claims to be running the world's first 800VDC data center in Ulanqab, China
stories.summary: Envision Digital has begun operating a facility in Inner Mongolia's Ulanqab region using 800VDC power architecture, claiming significant efficiency gains over conventional 400V or 240V systems. The higher voltage distribution reduces copper losses and enables more compact power infrastructure, though it requires specialized equipment and safety protocols not yet standardized across the industry.
stories.why_it_matters: Envision's 800VDC deployment, if validated at scale, could accelerate voltage standardization debates that have stalled industry-wide adoption of higher-efficiency power distribution. Chinese operators may gain first-mover cost advantages as domestic equipment suppliers optimize for 800VDC, while international operators face retrofit dilemmas or stranded asset risks if global standards diverge from China's technical trajectory.
stories.title_zh: 远景科技宣称在内蒙古乌兰察布运行全球首个800VDC数据中心
stories.summary_zh: Envision Digital已开始在内蒙Ulanqab地区使用800VDC电源架构运营设施，声称比传统的400V或240V系统有显著的效率提升。更高的电压分配减少了铜损并实现了更紧凑的电力基础设施，尽管它需要尚未在行业内标准化的专业设备和安全协议。
stories.why_zh: 如果在大规模上得到验证，Envision的800VDC部署可能会加速一直在阻碍行业范围内采用更高效率电力分配的标准化电压辩论。随着国内设备供应商优化800VDC，中国运营商可能获得先发成本优势，而国际运营商则面临改造困境或搁浅资产风险，如果全球标准与中国的技术轨迹出现分歧。
stories.content:
Green technology firm Envision claims to have built the world’s first 800VDC data center in Ulanqab, China.

The company said the 800VDC power system is running live compute workloads at its Galaxy AI data center in Ulanqab, which is part of Inner Mongolia. The size of the system running at the data center, which opened in August, has not been revealed.

A traditional data center power setup takes alternating current (AC) from the grid, and runs it through a series of conversion processes, first to direct current (DC) for the site’s battery or UPS, then back to AC to get it to the IT racks, then to DC to directly supply the server and its components.

800VDC systems promise to reduce this to a single conversion, from AC to DC, when power reaches the data center, then run the DC directly to the racks. This is seen as a way of getting more power into the server hall to meet the needs of future generations of AI hardware, which are likely to require much larger amounts of power than are currently available in data centers.

Envision said its newly deployed system combines solid-state transformers (SST), battery energy storage (BESS), and equipment that adjusts direct-current voltage for computing hardware. It has developed a controller known as Dubhe, supported by its own foundation AI model, Dubhe Energy, that coordinates the transformers and batteries in real time to match power supply with computing demand and manage sudden load swings.

According to the company, the SST converts 10kV medium voltage AC from the grid to an 800VDC busbar, which serves the hardware. An Open Compute Project white paper on 800VDC, released earlier this year, proposed using a busbar, cables, or a mixture of the two to transmit power to the servers.

“AI data centers need power systems that coordinate renewable energy, energy storage, and the grid to meet computing demand,” said Kevin Huang, senior vice president of Envision Energy and president of energy storage and AIDC Power Systems.

“Our integrated 800VDC system is now powering live computing workloads, demonstrating an end-to-end architecture that connects renewable energy supply with computing demand. This is a critical step in turning power-compute coordination from a strategic vision into an operational reality.”

The Galaxy AI data center will span 120,000 sqm (1.2m sq ft) and has a planned capacity of 3GW, it is designed to support up to one million AI accelerators, though the type of hardware it is currently running has not been disclosed. According to Envision, the data center is powered by 80 percent renewable energy.

Envision was founded in 2007 as a wind turbine company. The company says that it has installed 100GW of wind turbines, with 20GW installed globally in 2025. It hopes to bring 5GW of ‘green’ data center capacity online by 2030 as part of its Mission Gobi initiative.

*DCD* is not aware of any other data centers in the world running an 800VDC power setup, though many companies are working on SSTs which are likely to come to market in the next year.

Microsoft and Meta have proposed, through the OCP, designs for the Mount Diablo rack, which comes with a power sidecar enabling 400VDC to reach its servers.

*DCD took a deep dive into the world of 800VDC in the latest edition of our Magazine. Read it for freehere.*

stories.title: Digital Realty revenue hits $1.9bn, with a $2.5bn backlog
stories.summary: Digital Realty reported quarterly earnings of $1.9 billion, up 21 percent over the same time last year.
stories.title_zh: Digital Realty收入达19亿美元，积压订单25亿美元
stories.content:
Digital Realty reported quarterly earnings of $1.9 billion, up 21 percent over the same time last year.

The data center real estate investment trust (REIT) reported record overall leasing activity and strong growth in its interconnection business, but shares fell slightly on earnings.

Total leasing for the quarter was $855 million, with signings in the 0-1MW category (including interconnection) exceeding last quarter's record by 40 percent. Total greater-than-a-megawatt leasing reached $689m, "driven by a new high watermark in pricing," the company said.

Total hyperscale bookings of $689m were another record.

Digital Realty's total backlog similarly hit a new record of $2.5bn, including 2028 revenue.

"Demand was broad-based across geographies, customer segments and deployment types," CEO Andy Power said in an earnings call.

"In addition to two sizable hyperscale leases signed in early July in Northern Virginia, leasing was strong in APAC and exceeded our prior regional record by more than 600 percent."

CFO Matt Mercier added: "This quarter, the 500kW-1MW subsegment was particularly strong, driven by large enterprise and service provider deployments. We also saw a large network architecture deployment by one of the leading AI labs across 15 of our sites in EMEA.

"The sites serve as interconnection hubs, giving the customer direct private connectivity to cloud providers, network carriers and enterprise customers within each region."

Digital Realty spent $1.5 billion in development capex this past quarter, for a total of $3.3bn so far this year.

The company's development pipeline is 1.5GW under construction at a total expected cost of $22bn. The pipeline is 63 percent pre-leased.

Despite the revenue growth and total year guidance being raised, shares in the company fell amid broader uncertainty in the AI data center market.

"We have very little exposure, less than two percent, to some of the noise and names that people are worried about," Power said on CNBC, following concerns about neocloud debt.

stories.title: FuriosaAI raises $620m at a post-money valuation of approximately $2.9bn
stories.summary: FuriosaAI has raised $620 million in a Series D funding round, giving the company a post-money valuation of approximately $2.9 billion.
stories.title_zh: FuriosaAI融资6.2亿美元，投后估值约29亿美元
stories.content:
FuriosaAI has raised $620 million in a Series D funding round, giving the company a post-money valuation of approximately $2.9 billion.

South Korea's National Growth Fund was the largest investor, putting $280 million into the round. Meanwhile, international investors, including QUDA Capital Partners, Cisco Investments, NeoFort Holding, Jericho Capital, and Worldline Capital, contributed a total of $110 million.

The South Korean chip startup said the funds will be used to expand production of its RNGD chips, strengthen its software ecosystem, and accelerate development of its third-generation AI inference accelerator.

In May 2026, FuriosaAI announced it had partnered with Broadcom for the development of its third-generation AI accelerator, designed to support high-bandwidth, rack-scale networking across large AI compute clusters.

FuriosaAI added that it expects to produce 20,000 RNGD accelerators in 2026, with plans to more than double production to over 40,000 units in 2027 to support our growing customer demand.

“This Series D financing marks an important milestone for FuriosaAI and reflects the confidence of investors around the world in our technology and ability to execute,” said June Paik, co-founder and CEO of FuriosaAI. “We are particularly encouraged by the participation of investors with deep expertise and experience in the global AI semiconductor and infrastructure industries.”

He added: “We are entering a new phase of bringing our technology to the global AI infrastructure market at scale. By accelerating the commercialization of RNGD and advancing the development of Gen 3, we aim to help shape the next generation of AI infrastructure.”

Founded in 2017 and headquartered in South Korea's capital, Seoul, to date, FuriosaAI has raised approximately $115 million across four funding rounds to support the development of its RNGD chip. Furiosa’s 180W, PCIe-based RNGD accelerators are currently in mass production, fabricated on TSMC’s 5nm process node.

In March 2024, the startup turned down an $800m acquisition offer from Meta, reportedly because it wants to grow as an independent company instead. In January 2026, it was reported that FuriosaAI was seeking to raise between $300 and $500 million in a funding round ahead of its anticipated IPO.

stories.title: GE Vernova order backlog hits $197bn as data center demand drives gas turbine sales
stories.summary: US gas turbine manufacturer GE Vernova has seen its order book soar by 96 percent year on year, driven by skyrocketing demand from the data center sector.
stories.title_zh: GE Vernova订单积压达1970亿美元，数据中心需求推动gas turbine销售
stories.content:
US gas turbine manufacturer GE Vernova has seen its order book soar by 96 percent year on year, driven by skyrocketing demand from the data center sector.

The company revealed the order book in its Q3 earnings call, where it reported that its total backlog of orders had reached $197 billion, including $104bn in equipment backlog, up 92 percent, and $93bn in services backlog, up 14 percent.

CEO Scott Strazik said that the company now has around 100 gas power customers across 25 countries, of which 20 percent are data center customers. "Data centers require large electricity loads, driving the increasing need for more efficient high-voltage equipment," Strazik said.

The company said that it has signed 52GW of new gas turbine agreements so far this year, with Strazik stating that he expects the company to have at least 130GW under contract by the end of the year. This is an increase of 83GW from the start of last year.

The huge demand has led to price increases, with Q3 gas equipment orders priced more than 20 percent above Q4 2025 levels. Full-year 2026 gas pricing per kilowatt was said to be almost 50 percent above 2025.

This led the company to report a surge in revenue year on year, with Q3 revenue 18 percent higher than this time last year.

Demand from the data center sector has led to gas turbine orders to extend into the 2030s. This growth in demand led to warnings of a turbine supply shortage, with reports that manufacturers were facing delivery backlogs that stretched into the 2030s.

In addition to its gas turbine order book, the company also announced that it signed its first deployment deal for its medium-voltage UPS with an undisclosed hyperscaler. It also received a hyperscaler award for a 6MW outdoor solid-state transformer.

The company also announced the acquisition of Trench, a manufacturer of high-voltage grid components, for a reported $9bn. The deal is expected to close in late 2027.

It has also been investing in AI systems for its internal business operations. "We have investments in automation and AI with strong use cases that will expand margins over the medium term," Strazik said.

GE Vernova was formed in 2024 from the merger and subsequent spin-off of General Electric's energy businesses. It produces a range of energy equipment, including wind turbines and natural gas generators.

stories.title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman meets with Samsung execs as memory chip shortage deepens
stories.summary: Sam Altman held discussions with Samsung Electronics executives in Seoul as OpenAI scrambles to secure stable supplies of high-bandwidth memory chips critical for training large AI models. The meeting underscores deepening supply chain anxiety as HBM3E and future HBM4 production remains concentrated among Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron.
stories.why_it_matters: Altman's direct engagement with Samsung reveals how AI model providers are bypassing traditional component distributors to lock up memory supply at the source. Cloud providers and GPU server manufacturers without similar executive-level access face allocation disadvantages, potentially widening the competitive gap between OpenAI-backed infrastructure and rival AI platforms.
stories.title_zh: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman会见Samsung高管，因memory chip短缺加剧
stories.summary_zh: Sam Altman在首尔与Samsung Electronics高管举行了会谈，因为OpenAI急于确保训练大型AI模型所需的高带宽内存芯片的稳定供应。这次会议凸显了日益加深的供应链焦虑，因为HBM3E和未来HBM4的生产仍然集中在Samsung、SK Hynix和Micron手中。
stories.why_zh: Altman与Samsung的直接接触揭示了AI模型提供商如何绕过传统组件分销商，在源头锁定内存供应。没有类似高管级别访问权限的云提供商和GPU服务器制造商面临分配劣势，可能会扩大OpenAI支持的基础设施与竞争AI平台之间的差距。
stories.content:
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has met with top executives from Samsung in an effort to shore up its supply of memory chips amid ongoing shortages.

Per a report from Bloomberg, Altman met with around 50 senior executives from the South Korean chipmaker in Yongin, south of Seoul, to discuss the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on industries such as finance and biotech, and potential business opportunities over the coming decade.

The discussions took place in the same week that the OpenAI CEO appeared on the Cheeky Pint podcast, where he told the host – Stripe co-founder John Collison – that individuals using their desktop computers to do local inference were further constraining memory chip supply chains.

“A lot of people want local inference, and somehow, they assume that the problem is solved now, because we are going to have open-source models,” Altman said.

“\[They think\] ‘We’re going to be able to run them on our computers and so we’re not going to need all the stuff in the data center.’“

He continued: “But, from a global allocation perspective, actually, it's quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world's limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer and being used five percent of the time. You want maximum utilization in the cloud if you're trying to deal with this very supply-constrained environment. And somehow many people's intuition is the opposite of that."

Memory companies have warned that the memory chip shortage is likely to persist into 2027 and beyond, with consumer electronics the most likely to suffer in the face of ongoing shortages, as capacity will increasingly become allocated to AI infrastructure projects.

In January 2025, the Wall Street Journal reported that data from TrendForce shows that up to 70 percent of the memory produced worldwide in 2026 will be consumed by data centers.

In October 2025, OpenAI signed a letter of intent (LOI) with Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix for the supply of memory chips.

At the time, the companies released a statement claiming OpenAI’s Stargate memory demand was projected to reach 900,000 DRAM wafers a month, although no timeline was given for when that demand was expected to be met.

No further details regarding the agreement or anticipated DRAM allocation have been provided by either company. However, in September of this year, following comments from Harrison Kim, general manager of OpenAI Korea, that Samsung was working with OpenAI on the development of next-generation chips, a spokesperson for OpenAI said the partners were simply planning to expand their collaboration “in the context of our existing relationship, including Samsung Electronics’ adoption of ChatGPT and the LOI announced last October.”

stories.title: Rolling with the punches: NextDC braces for another strike against pay
stories.summary: The hits keep on coming at Craig Scroggie-led data centre owner NextDC. And another blow may be delivered in just 18 days if the company’s board has not manoeuvred strategically and swiftly enough to…
stories.title_zh: 迎难而上：NextDC准备应对又一轮薪酬罢工
stories.content:
The hits keep on coming at Craig Scroggie-led data centre owner NextDC. And another blow may be delivered in just 18 days if the company’s board has not manoeuvred strategically and swiftly enough to avoid a second strike against pay at its upcoming annual shareholder meeting.

Influential governance firm CGI Glass Lewis is already urging investors to vote against NextDC’s remuneration report. That’s based on what CGI deems an inadequate response by the board to last year’s strike, recent operational woes, and a stark misalignment between remuneration and performance.

stories.title: LG CNS completes 30 MW AI data center in Jakarta
stories.summary: The SMX01 facility in Cibitung represents a rare Korean-Indonesian joint venture in data center infrastructure, combining LG CNS's operational expertise with SM Group's local market access. The 21 MW initial phase targets financial services and cloud customers seeking AI-ready colocation with direct connectivity to major Indonesian network exchanges.
stories.why_it_matters: LG CNS's Indonesian entry demonstrates how Korean technology groups are diversifying data center investments beyond their domestic market as Seoul's grid constraints tighten. Indonesian enterprises gain access to international-standard AI infrastructure without relying solely on Singapore-based facilities, while the KIRA involvement signals Korean institutional capital's growing appetite for Southeast Asian digital infrastructure as an asset class distinct from traditional real estate.
stories.title_zh: LG CNS完成雅加达30MW AI数据中心建设
stories.summary_zh: 位于Cibitung的SMX01设施代表了韩国-印尼在data centre基础设施中罕见的合资企业，结合了LG CNS的运营专业知识和SM Group的本地市场准入。21 MW的初始阶段面向寻求AI-ready colocation并与主要印尼网络交换中心直接连接的金融服务业和云客户。
stories.why_zh: LG CNS进入印尼表明，随着首尔电网限制收紧，韩国科技集团如何将其data centre投资多元化到国内市场之外。印尼企业无需仅依赖新加坡的设施即可获得国际标准AI基础设施，而KIRA的参与则标志着韩国机构资本对东南亚数字基础设施作为区别于传统房地产的资产类别日益增长的兴趣。
stories.content:
LG CNS, a South Korean digital transformation and information technology services company, has completed construction of a 30 MW AI data center in Jakarta, Indonesia. The project was commissioned by Kuningan Mas Gemilang (KMG), a joint venture between Indonesia’s Cinarmas Group and South Korea’s Tuzarial Asset Management.

According to an LG CNS press release, the facility is designed to support high performance computing (HPC) using next generation graphics processing units (GPUs) and marks the first time a South Korean company has directly built an AI data center overseas for a local customer.

Hyun Shin-kyun, CEO, LG CNS, said, “Completion of the construction of the Indonesian AI data center will provide LG CNS’s domestically accumulated data center capabilities to overseas customers. It is a meaningful achievement that has proven business competitiveness in the global market. We will use this as a bridgehead to expand our AI data center and AI factory business in global markets, including the Asia-Pacific region, where demand for AI computing is rapidly increasing.”

The data center’s power infrastructure can support loads exceeding 300 KW per rack, allowing it to accommodate multiple GPUs within a single rack. Redundant power systems, including backup supplies, are designed to maintain operations around the clock in the event of a disruption to the main electricity supply. Its cooling infrastructure combines air cooling with provisions for liquid cooling, which will be introduced in a subsequent construction phase to manage the heat generated by high density AI servers.

Once completed, the data center’s total capacity is expected to reach 400 MW, positioning it among Indonesia’s largest AI data center facilities. The project also brought together capabilities from across the LG Group, including LG Electronics’ air conditioning systems and LG Energy Solution’s batteries, alongside LG CNS’ data center design, construction and operation expertise.

LG CNS is also pursuing AI data center projects in other Asia-Pacific markets, including Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, the Philippines and Japan, using its Indonesian project as a reference for overseas expansion.

Beyond data center construction and operation, LG CNS has been expanding into modular data centers, GPU-as-a-Service (GPUaaS) and liquid cooling infrastructure. The company also plans to develop AI factory services that integrate AI platforms and infrastructure.

stories.title: South Korea sets aside US$15.8 billion for AI data centers and chips in record 2027 budget
stories.summary: The KRW 820.9 trillion budget proposal allocates substantially increased funding toward AI data centers, domestic semiconductor manufacturing, and supporting digital infrastructure. The nearly 100% year-over-year increase in AI-related physical infrastructure spending reflects President Lee's campaign commitment to position South Korea as a leading AI nation.
stories.why_it_matters: Seoul's fiscal commitment intensifies the regional subsidy arms race for semiconductor and AI infrastructure investment, forcing Taiwan, Japan, and China to match or exceed these incentives. Korean chaebols including Samsung and SK Group gain predictable domestic demand visibility, while foreign equipment vendors and hyperscalers seeking Korean capacity face more competitive local bidding environments.
stories.title_zh: 韩国在创纪录的2027年预算中拨款158亿美元用于AI数据中心和芯片
stories.summary_zh: KRW 820.9万亿的预算提案大幅增加对AI data centers、国内半导体制造和支持性数字基础设施的资金。AI相关物理基础设施支出同比近100%的增长反映了Lee Jae Myung总统将韩国定位为领先AI国家的竞选承诺。
stories.why_zh: 首尔的财政承诺加剧了半导体和AI基础设施投资的地区补贴军备竞赛，迫使台湾、日本和中国匹配或超越这些激励措施。包括Samsung和SK Group在内的韩国财阀获得了可预测的国内需求可见性，而寻求韩国产能的外国设备供应商和hyperscalers面临更具竞争力的本地竞标环境。
stories.content:
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung revealed the country’s largest ever budget for 2027 with spending on digital infrastructure, including physical artificial intelligence (AI), AI data centers, and semiconductors set to nearly double compared to 2026.

Speaking to the National Assembly on Monday, Lee announced that total spending would rise 12.8 percent to KRW 820.9 trillion (US$ 610.14 billion). Of that figure, CNBC reports that KRW 21.3 trillion (US$ 15.83 billion) has been set aside for physical AI, AI data centers, and semiconductors. A further KRW 4.7 trillion (US$ 3.5 billion) has been earmarked to develop a sovereign AI model.

“It is not enough for the national economy to simply grow. Those outcomes must connect to opportunities and changes in the lives of each and every citizen. We will create opportunities for youth to take on challenges, provide small business owners with the strength to rise again, and build new engines of growth for our regions,” the president said in a statement posted to X.

The South Korean government will also train 2,000 specialists to lead semiconductor design and the wider chip industry. Students at some South Korean universities will be given the opportunity to enroll in company-linked degrees that provide a pathway to employment at the likes of Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix.

South Korea’s Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources reported on Sunday, November 1, that monthly exports had hit an all-time high, with cumulative exports for the year so far surpassing US$ 900 billion. Semiconductors posted the highest exports for any October on record. The President said that the country was within reach of achieving US$ 1 trillion in annual exports.

Importantly, Lee has said that the increased government spending for 2027 would result in virtually no net increase in government debt as it would lean on newly issued bonds to repay existing debt.

In June, President Lee announced three megaprojects aimed at strengthening South Korea’s competitiveness in advanced technologies. Among the projects is a national AI data center program, which includes an 8.4 GW facility set to be built by 2029 in partnership with the private sector.
